text: A hundred and twenty metres up a shooting gallery. Jaeha crosses that plan out.
Uncle Pyo taps the page. Halfway up, a sludge mouth opens on the canyon, across from the rim ledge. But the walkway fell years ago. It's a forty-metre gap.
Jaeha turns to Moon Ahin, and she already knows. He wants a bridge. Tonight her husks have been a wall and a door. They can be a bridge.
She raises her baton. Get them halfway up first. Then they'll see.
Borro, back in field form, charges up the walkway, everyone packed behind his cracked shield.
Twelve carbines open up from the top, and the bolts hammer his shield.
Lyra fires back over it, arrow after arrow.
Jaeha carries both, and every bolt on that shield jolts through him.
A crossbow bolt pins Ho to the wall by his tabard. She missed on purpose, he insists. She winked at him.
Then Nib dives into the sludge mouth, and everyone pours in after him.
Borro backs in last, his shield taking one final volley.
Up top, Sora grins. There's nothing in that sludge mouth but a drop. She sends her squad to the rim ledge.
The sludge tunnel ends on a narrow lip of stone, high on the open canyon face.
And there it is. Across forty metres of empty air, the gate's rim, a tall ellipse of white light, Kanghan's steel iris closing round it. Five minutes twelve.
Home is right there, Dami whispers. With forty metres of nothing in between, says Ho.
Moon Ahin counts it out. Thirty husks. Forty metres. And everyone on their backs.
Jaeha tells her quietly she can say no. They're hers.
That surprises her.
She lays a hand on Number One's blank face, something she has never done before an order. Take the far end. And don't let go of her.
Then she conducts with both arms, fierce and alight, and her husks leap into the air one after another, each catching the ankles of the one before.
The chain reaches the far side, and Number One locks onto the old walkway stump.
A sagging lattice of white husks spans the abyss, creaking and swaying.
Jaeha calls it the most beautiful thing he's ever seen. Walk, Number Four, she tells him. Before she thinks about it.
Nib runs across first, light as a cat. Dami follows, arms out for balance.
Woo and Ho cross hand in hand. Then Borro steps on with Uncle Pyo, and the bridge groans.
One husk cracks under his weight and falls away into three hundred metres of air.
Moon Ahin flinches, and drives the baton on. Twenty-nine.
Cracks spider across the husks, and Borro freezes in the middle, afraid to take another step.
Jaeha watches the cracks. Her husks are summoned, like his. Empty, but summoned. So maybe...
A window. Link: twenty-nine husks, summoner Moon Ahin. The husks do not refuse. Carry them?
Nobody has ever carried them. Not once.
Twenty-nine white threads run from Jaeha into the bridge. The cracks stop. Bruises bloom up his arms and neck. Carry load: two hundred and forty percent. Critical.
Moon Ahin sees her husks stop cracking, and the same cracks bloom as bruises on his arms. Why is he carrying her husks? Because they are carrying us.
Her composure breaks, and she turns to the bridge so he won't see her eyes.
Borro moves again, and this time the husks hold. Nib pulls Woo and Ho onto the ledge.
Then a side door bangs open on the rim ledge, and eight troopers pour out.
Lyra shoots the first carbine over the edge. Nobody shoots at her bridge!
Moon Ahin doesn't look round. Her bridge?
She's standing on the end of it, says Lyra. That makes it partly hers.
Nib leaps off the far end into the troopers, field form, no carry.
He goes through them like a gust of wind, and still hauls one trooper back from the edge.
The crew and Borro make it onto the ledge, and Jaeha lets Borro's link go to carry the husks. Three minutes ten.
Lyra runs the bridge, light and fast, turning mid-stride to shoot back.
That leaves Jaeha and Moon Ahin. If she stops conducting, the husks fall. So she'll conduct while she walks. She's very good.
They step onto the bridge together, her right arm conducting, her left holding him up.
Through his greying eyes: cracked white backs, empty air, and his own blood dripping onto a husk.
A husk cracks right across under his foot but holds, and he stumbles toward the edge. She hauls him upright by the tabard without missing a beat.
A bruise blooms across his forearm in the exact shape of the crack.
Don't you dare faint on her husks, Number Four. He wouldn't dream of it, ma'am.
On the ledge, Nib waves them on. Hurry! The rim is narrower than a man now.
Three-quarters of the way. Two minutes four.
And while everyone watches Jaeha, a black boot steps onto Number One's back.
Han Sora stands on the end of the bridge, crossbow raised, the white light behind her: cold, beautiful, and blocking the only way home.
Hello again, Operator. Now hold still.
They stop dead. The baton freezes. Even the husks hold their breath.
Her eye along the sights is perfectly steady.
The bolt is aimed dead at the T-4 stencilled on his chest.
Jaeha looks straight down the bolt and smiles politely. Good evening, Miss Han. She's standing on a very brave husk.
One minute fifty-eight, a crossbow on his heart, and three hundred metres of air below.
